feature: Make Component and a panel menu on the Layers header
summary: The Layers header now carries a layer count, a Make Component button and a panel menu (Group Selection, Make Component, Hide This Panel), as both component mocks draw it. Picking a group and pressing the button does exactly what Option Command K does.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/layers-header-make-component-walk.json

try.do: File > New, Blank canvas. Draw a rectangle and an ellipse.
Select both and press Command G. The Layers header reads 4 and its component button lights up.
Press the four-diamond button at the right end of the Layers header.
Check the row now reads Component, Copy with the violet mark, the canvas shows the badge, and the Library opened on the new tile.
Press Command Z. It is a plain group again and the count is back to 4.
Click the three dots on the Layers header and read the three rows and their keys.
Switch to the light scheme and look at the header again.
Pick Hide This Panel from the three dots. Option Command L brings the panel back.

evaluate: Is the four-diamond button on the header the place you would reach for to make a component, after picking a group?
Does the count beside LAYERS mean what you expect: every layer, the contents of groups included?
Is it clear enough when the button is dimmed (nothing picked, or a copy picked) that it cannot act right now?
Is Hide This Panel worth having in this menu when the title bar button and Option Command L already do it?
rough: Side by side with component-configure-wt.html (#gLayersH, picture 2026-10-08-layers-header-mock-configure.png) and components.html (#layerMenu, 2026-10-08-layers-header-mock-components.png): title, count chip, button and dots sit in the mock's order and match it in dark and light (crops in 2026-10-08-layers-header-crops.png).
The count chip matches the mock (#layerCount); it counts every layer the list could show, groups' contents included, the same total the find field counts against.
The button's icon matches the mock's line icon: the app's four-diamond component glyph in outline, in the header's ink.
The menu rows match the mock's #layerMenu: its three icons, its keys and a divider above Hide This Panel.
Make Component from this button behaves exactly as Option Command K does, including opening the Library on the new tile with its name ready to type.
